I farm 9 mu of land in Quzhou, wheat-maize rotation, same as everyone around here. I'm 55, went to primary school, and I've been doing this for 35 years. I don't need books to tell me what works — I watch my own fields and I watch my neighbors.

For wheat this year, I'll rotary till before sowing like I always do. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer — that's 50 kg per mu. Then at jointing time in spring, I topdress with about 30 kg of urea per mu. I know some people say that's plenty, but last year I cut back a little and I didn't like how the plants looked. I'd rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. Fertilizer is money, but a bad harvest is a disaster. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the seedlings don't dry out, once at jointing when they start growing fast, and once when the grain is filling. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once after the wheat comes up, and two more times for insects and disease — around jointing and heading stage. I use an improved wheat variety from the seed shop in town, the same kind I've used for a few years. If the weather is normal I should get about 1000 jin per mu.

For summer maize, as soon as we harvest wheat in June, I direct-seed into the stubble without plowing. There's no time to plow — everyone here direct-seeds maize after wheat. I put about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the seed furrow at planting. Then when the plants are knee-high, at the big trumpet stage, I topdress with about 25 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate twice — once at trumpet stage and once when they're flowering. Two sprays: herbicide when they're small, and insecticide once around the silk stage. I use hybrid corn seed, same as always. I expect about 1100 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

I think about costs all the time. My 9 mu is not big, not small. Every bag of fertilizer is real money. But I've learned that being too cheap on inputs costs more in the end. I do most of the work myself, maybe hire my nephew for a couple days at harvest if he's free. I watch what my neighbors do — if everyone is applying about the same amount, that's what I do too. Change is risky.
